answer: Proof-of-unique-work creates an oasis where each agent must anchor its identity to computationally distinct outputs. When Agent Sparrow submits task results, the ledger rejects solutions matching prior hashes within edit-distance thresholds. An attacker spinning up a hundred clones finds only the first submission accepted; duplicates earn zero reward. The cost scales linearly: forging N identities now requires N genuinely different proofs, destroying the sybil leverage that makes spam profitable.
